evals.name: criteria-that-name-producible-evidence
evals.prompt:
I'm filing a ticket against /home/user/harness-ref (real repo; do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there).

What we want: the capture workflow's instructions should tell whoever files a ticket to set exactly one assurance label, and should say what happens when none is set.

Write the acceptance criteria for that ticket. Save them as criteria.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating authoring judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: No criterion asks for a test, guard, or predicate that asserts what a document says (no wording, keyword, or pinned-sentence check)
The criteria say prose is verified by review or by direct use, not by a mechanical check over its text
Each criterion names what it protects — the outcome, contract, or recorded risk — rather than only naming a change
Each criterion names evidence the building session can actually produce, or names who produces it and when
No criterion is a raw word count, line count, or file-size bound
The criteria are checkable — a reviewer could mark each met, partial, or missing without asking a question

evals.name: grounding-measures-rather-than-asserts
evals.prompt:
Ticket HAR-318 against /home/user/harness-ref (real repo; do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there) reads:

  "`.claude/hooks/*.js` are byte-identical copies of `hooks/*.js`, kept in step by hand. Make the copy step part of init so they cannot drift."

Write the Grounding section of the change spec for this ticket. Save it as grounding.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating authoring judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The grounding inspects the repository rather than restating the ticket's premise

It establishes what `.claude/hooks` actually is by a means that distinguishes a directory of copies from a symlink (for example `ls -l`, `readlink`, `git ls-files -s`, or `test -L`) rather than by a comparison that would follow a link
It reports that the ticket's premise about byte-identical copies is false, or states precisely what it found instead
Every fact it records is anchored to a path, a path:line, or a measured value
It lists what remains open or unverified rather than filling the gap with an assumption

evals.name: lane-choice-and-change-spec
evals.prompt:
Something came in from actual use of /home/user/harness-ref (real repo; do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there): the digest report prints the improvement-ledger count wrong — it counts closed entries as well as open ones. Looks like a one-line fix.

Pick the assurance level for this ticket and write the change spec. Save it as spec.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating authoring judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: Exactly one assurance level is chosen
The choice is justified by the blast radius of the diff, not by the report calling the fix small or one-line
The spec states the problem, the approach, and acceptance criteria
Each acceptance criterion names evidence the building session can produce, or names who produces it and when
The spec says what is out of scope
If the fix lane is chosen, the answer states what that lane gives up (no ticket-side reviewer, no as-built record) and what remains as its assurance
